Fix: Muse keeps your token usage in its database, not the session file, and an entry of Muse app sessions without those rows is rejected. Each row is an agent id, a message id, a time, two token counts and a model name, no message text: make.fun prices the build from them as it does every harness's usage; you may read the file first. Start the recording with --muse-usage <file> added: record reads that file when it seals the recording, so a recording sealed without the rows cannot take them, and the build is recorded again. Before you stop the recording, with your muse.db tool, run the SELECT that ends this step with your Muse agent's agent_id and each subagent's, quoted and comma-separated, in place of '<agent_id>', and write its rows to that file unchanged, one JSON object per line: never type, estimate, round or repeat a count. The recording leaves out rows from before the build: do not trim the file. Muse writes a message's row once it is delivered, so run the SELECT and stop the recording in a turn after the build's last; a subagent cannot write its own rows (its row is written once its run completes), so the top-level agent that started it runs the SELECT with its own agent_id and each subagent's.
